q: Who is credited with the dictum "God is in the details"?
n: The aphorism is attributed to Mies van der Rohe.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Modern Movement, Mies van der Rohe

q: Who is credited with the dictum "Less is more"?
n: "Less is more" is the best-known maxim of Mies van der Rohe and of minimalist modernism.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Modern Movement, Mies van der Rohe

q: Who countered with the dictum "Less is a bore"?
n: Venturi's postmodern reply appears in Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture.
ref: Venturi, Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture (MoMA, 1966), Ch. 1

q: Who is credited with the dictum "To create, one must question everything"?
n: The quotation is attributed to the Irish designer and architect Eileen Gray.
ref: Attributed to Eileen Gray (Irish architect and designer, 1878-1976)

q: Who is credited with the dictum "Form ever follows function"?
n: Louis Sullivan coined the phrase. Wright, his protégé, later recast it as "form and function are one".
ref: Sullivan, 'The Tall Office Building Artistically Considered', Lippincott's Magazine, March 1896

q: Which of the following is NOT a principle of design?
n: The listed principles are proportion, scale, contrast, balance, hierarchy, rhythm and unity. Line is an element of design.
ref: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order, 4th ed. - Principles of Ordering

q: Which principle of design refers to the size of an element relative to a known reference, such as the human body?
n: Scale compares size to a reference such as the human figure. Proportion compares the parts of a composition to one another and to the whole.
ref: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order, 4th ed. - Proportion and Scale

q: In standard anthropometric data, what average standing height is used for an adult female?
n: Anthropometric tables put the adult female average standing height near 1.63 m (5'4"); the adult male average is about 1.75 m (5'9").
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - standing body dimensions, adult female

q: Which of the following is NOT a primary color?
n: The traditional primaries are red, yellow and blue. Orange is a secondary, made from red and yellow.
ref: Itten, The Art of Color - RYB primaries; Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order, 4th ed. - Color

q: What is the average standing height of an adult Filipino male?
n: FNRI-DOST survey data put the adult Filipino male mean height at about 163 cm. The international design figure of 1.75 m is taller, so check whose data the question uses.
ref: FNRI-DOST National Nutrition Survey - anthropometric data, Filipino adults

q: What is the average standing height of an adult Filipino female?
n: FNRI-DOST survey data put the adult Filipino female mean height at about 151.5 cm.
ref: FNRI-DOST National Nutrition Survey - anthropometric data, Filipino adults

q: What is the average weight of an adult Filipino male?
n: FNRI-DOST survey data put the adult Filipino male mean weight at about 61.3 kg.
ref: FNRI-DOST National Nutrition Survey - anthropometric data, Filipino adults

q: What is the average weight of an adult Filipino female?
n: FNRI-DOST survey data put the adult Filipino female mean weight at about 54.3 kg.
ref: FNRI-DOST National Nutrition Survey - anthropometric data, Filipino adults

q: In standard anthropometric data, what average standing height is used for an adult male?
n: Anthropometric tables put the adult male average standing height near 1.75 m (5'9"), against 1.63 m (5'4") for the adult female.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - standing body dimensions, adult male
